Paragraph: Some of them sacrifice the hearing process and the senses in the fire of the controlled mind, and others sacrifice the objects of the senses, such as sound, in the fire of sacrifice.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Managing sensory overload, external distractions, and uncurbed desires that compromise mental clarity.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'Some of them sacrifice the hearing process and the senses in the fire of the controlled mind, and others sacrifice the objects of the senses, such as sound, in the fire of sacrifice.'
Outcome/Resolution: Restraining sensory intake or regulating sense interactions purifies the mind and deepens self-control.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Sensory Regulation: Managing exposure to external stimuli to prevent cognitive overload
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mindful Input Control: Filtering the information and influences allowed into one's consciousness
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Disciplined Self-Restraint: Practicing intentional moderation over sensory desires

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Srotradinindriyany anye samyamagnisu juhvati (Sacrificing hearing and senses in the fire of mental control)
Sabdadin visayan anya indriyagnisu juhvati (Sacrificing sensory objects like sound into the fire of regulated senses)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Whether through celibate restraint or regulated family life, offering sensory activities as a sacrifice purifies consciousness.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Filtering sensory inputs protects mental health from chaotic external influences and reinforces self-discipline.
